_description: Per-scheme upper bounds on the COMMUTATIVE exponent ω_c, defined as the smallest constant such that ⟨n,n,n⟩ matmul over a commutative ring can be done in O(n^ω_c) operations. Each entry is a single-shape claim of the form ω_c ≤ log_n(R_c(n)) derived from a published commutative-only construction. CAVEAT: unlike NC ω (see omega-history.json), commutative algorithms do NOT lift to recursive matrix matmul over non-commutative rings — block recursion fails because matrices don't commute. So each entry below is a fixed-n upper bound, not an asymptotically-aggregated exponent in the NC sense. See FUTURE_WORK.md §'Commutative asymptotic exponent ω_c' for the subtleties; the Islam 2009 MSc thesis (`references/papers/islam_2009_msc_optim_matmul.pdf`) discusses the recursion-for-commutative argument more carefully than this catalog entry can.

_schema.year: year of public announcement (preprint or proceedings, whichever first)
_schema.omega_c_upper: log_n(rank) — single-shape upper bound on the commutative exponent
_schema.scheme_file: catalog file providing the explicit construction (relative to src/main/resources/schemes/), or null if rank-only claim

lower_bound_source: information-theoretic — n² output entries cannot be produced in fewer than n² operations; same lower bound as NC ω

entries.method: Strassen ⟨2,2,2⟩ (NC scheme; valid over any commutative ring)
entries.notes: log_2(7). Strassen's algorithm works over any ring; usable commutatively too. Defied attack for ~7 years even in the commutative setting.

log_4(46). Generic formula (n²+2n−1)·⌊n/2⌋+(n%2)·n² applied at n=4. Strictly commutative — does not lift to matrix block recursion. Waksman's n=3 case (rank 23) yields log_3(23)=2.854, dominated by Strassen even commutatively.

log_6(141). Same Waksman formula at n=6 — comparable to n=4. Waksman's series log_n(R_c(n)) does NOT tend to a sub-3 limit; the curve has a local minimum near n=4–6 and rises back toward 3 for large n. See ROADMAP / FUTURE_WORK for the asymptotic-claim discussion.
log_3(23). First explicit ⟨3,3,3⟩=23. Tied with Waksman 1970 ⟨3,3,3⟩=23 at base shape; both above Strassen's 2.807 even commutatively.
log_3(22). First commutative-only improvement at ⟨3,3,3⟩. Paper is in Russian; explicit factor matrices not yet located — only the rank claim is registered (docs/cited-bounds.json).

log_3(21). First explicit commutative ⟨3,3,3⟩=21 in published literature. Bit-distinct from RosowskiAlgorithm1 specialised to n=3 (same rank, different product indexing). Beats Strassen's 2.807 only at this single base shape; does NOT beat Waksman ⟨4,4,4⟩ in single-shape ω_c.
